subject: Clarify retention TTLs & deletion proof for SOC 2 / ISO audit
messages:
From: Ellen Zhao <ellen.zhao@clearharbor.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: Jim Patel <jim.patel@compliance-partners.io>

Subject: Retention TTLs + deletion proof for SOC 2 / ISO audit

Hi Mateo,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our audit team following up with a short list of questions focused on data retention and deletion evidence (SOC 2 / ISO scope). I've attached the questionnaire as a PDF. High-level asks:

- What are the default retention TTLs for PII contained in request logs and embeddings?
- How do you prove an object was deleted (audit trail / immutable logs)?
- How do backups and snapshots affect deletion guarantees (esp. for EU-residency workloads)?
- Do you provide a canonical export showing deletion events we can hand to auditors?

Can you (or someone from compliance) respond with the specific artifacts we can reference in our evidence packet? Also tagging Jim from our compliance vendor in case he has extra requirements.

Best,
Ellen

Attachment: clearharbor_retention_questions.pdf (PDF, 27KB)
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Ellen Zhao <ellen.zhao@clearharbor.com>
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 19 Aug 2026 11:06:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Retention TTLs + deletion proof for SOC 2 / ISO audit

Hi Ellen — thanks for the clear list. I've pasted concise answers below and attached a short runbook + sample deletion log export. Mina (Security) and Soojin (Compliance) are cc'd for any technical addenda.

Summary answers (short):
- Default retention TTLs:
  • Request metadata & logs: 90 days (default), configurable per-account down to 30 days or up to 3 years under contract.
  • Embeddings & derived vectors: 180 days default; customers may opt-in to longer retention for analytics (documented in console).
  • Backups / snapshots: 30 days on warm snapshots; 365 days for cold backups if configured by customer.
- Deletion proof: We provide an auditable deletion event export that includes timestamp, object id, region, actor (service principal), and verification checksum. Each deletion emits an immutable event to the audit stream (append-only) and a secondary signed tombstone entry.
- Backups & snapshots: Deletion from primary store triggers asynchronous retention reconciliation for snapshots/backups. For EU-residency-enabled projects we pin backup locations to the region and run a separate retention GC that respects region residency.
- Canonical export: Attached: "deletion_audit_log_20260730.csv" is an example export; we can deliver a filtered export for auditor ingestion.

Next steps:
1) Mina will provide more detail on the retention GC and sample queries you can run against the audit stream.
2) We can produce a time-bounded export for ClearHarbor's auditor (format CSV + signed manifest).
3) If you need, we can schedule a 30-min call to walk through the logs and export.

Attachments: runbook_deletion_workflow_v2.md, deletion_audit_log_20260730.csv

Regards,
Mateo

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Ellen Zhao <ellen.zhao@clearharbor.com>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>

Date: Wed, 19 Aug 2026 13:38:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Retention TTLs + deletion proof for SOC 2 / ISO audit

Ellen — adding technical detail on deletion workflow and evidence artifacts. Short version first, then example queries and caveats.

How deletion works (technical):
- Logical delete: API call marks object state=deleted in metadata store, emits deletion event to our append-only audit stream (Kafka topic encrypted at rest), and enqueues the object id for GC.
- Asynchronous physical removal: Background GC workers process GC queue and remove objects from primary object store (S3/GCS or on-prem NFS) and purge KV caches.
- Snapshot/backups: For cloud-hosted snapshots we keep separate retention configs. When an object is removed from primary, the snapshot GC either overwrites the snapshot manifest or marks the blob as expired; cold backups are retained per customer config and require an explicit retention override to delete early.
- Proof: Deletion event record schema includes: event_id, object_id, timestamp_utc, principal, region, combined_hash. Events are immutably stored in a write-once ledger for 7 years (readable by auditors with signed requests). We sign daily manifests with our HSM key so auditors can verify integrity.

Example audit queries (we will run for you):
- Count of deletions for object prefix: SELECT count(*) FROM audit_stream WHERE object_id LIKE 'cbh-1234-%' AND event_type='DELETE' AND timestamp BETWEEN '2026-07-01' AND '2026-07-31';
- Export fields: object_id,timestamp_utc,principal,region,combined_hash,event_id,signed_manifest_id

Caveats & regional notes:
- EU-residency projects: backups are pinned; GC runs in-region. If customer enabled cross-region DR, copies exist in DR region and are subject to separate GC windows — we'll include those in the export.
- For on-prem/private deployments: deletion physically removes files per customer policy; our runbook documents secure erase steps and key-handling for encrypted volumes.

Attached is the deletion runbook and a sample export (redacted). If auditors need schema-level definitions or sample signed manifests, we can provide them under an NDA.

-Mina
Director, Product Security

Thanks — this is helpful. A couple clarifying items from our auditor:

1) Can you confirm the signature scheme for the daily manifests (algorithm + key rotation cadence)? Auditor needs to reference algorithm in their control mapping.
2) For the append-only ledger: is there read-only access for auditors or do you provide read-exported manifests only?

If you can provide short answers to those two items and an ETA for the filtered export we can schedule the evidence upload window.

Best,
Ellen
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Ellen Zhao <ellen.zhao@clearharbor.com>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>

Date: Fri, 21 Aug 2026 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Retention TTLs + deletion proof for SOC 2 / ISO audit

Hi Ellen — quick follow-up with the two items:

1) Signature scheme: we sign daily manifests with RSA-4096 using PKCS#1 v1.5 and SHA-256. Keys are stored in our HSM and rotated on a 12-month cadence; emergency rotation is documented in our KMS key management SOP (we can supply the SOP excerpt). Manifests include manifest_id, date, signed_hash, and public_key_fingerprint.

2) Ledger access: auditors do not get direct console read access to the append-only ledger. We provide signed exported manifests and a time-bounded CSV export (signed manifest + verification checksum). Exports include a signed manifest for the export itself (signed by HSM) so auditors can verify integrity without needing direct access. For long-term engagements we can set up an auditor API token with read-only access under a scoped contract.

ETA for filtered export: 48 business hours once you confirm the object prefixes / time window. We'll prepare CSV + signed manifest and upload to the Drive folder noted in the related links.

Happy to hop on a 30-min call if the auditor prefers a walkthrough.

Thanks,
Soojin Lee
Staff Compliance Manager, Redwood Inference
